title: Study Assistant extension SDK
description: Authoring and operating Study Assistant's extension surface over the family extension charter: the bundled connectors (external sources, discovery, MCP servers), the vendored ADR-0035 web-search trio, per-tool discovery/parse contracts with keyring-sealed secrets, and the T3 MCP instance lifecycle.

roots.title: Overview
roots.description: What the extension surface is — connectors feeding a dual-mode desktop product's discovery and import pipelines — and when to build an extension instead of a core feature.

roots.title: Quickstart
roots.description: Register an MCP server modeled on the family template, refresh to list its real tools, declare the discovery contract, and watch DISCOVER use it — with a real transcript.

roots.title: Core Concepts
roots.description: The load-bearing nouns: extension, instance, tool contract, provider, source, suggestion, consent — and the vendored-contract discipline that keeps them honest.

roots.title: Installation & Modes
roots.description: Connecting sources and servers in the app: the Tools tab surfaces, the disclosure box, and what enabled means.

children.title: Install lifecycle internals
children.description: Desktop vs web modes, where preferences and secrets live on disk, and the bundled-catalog steady state.

children.title: Add a search provider
children.description: Configure the web search behind chat research and discovery — Tavily, SearXNG, Brave, Exa, Serper or Google PSE, keys in the keyring.

children.title: Manage web sources
children.description: RSS feeds, YouTube channels and playlists, and site-filtered searches that suggest new material on a schedule.

roots.title: Authoring & Configuration
roots.description: The MCP registration shape (transports, per-tool contracts, url_patterns), the web-search provider config, and external-source kinds with their envelope manifests.

roots.title: Examples & Use Cases
roots.description: Five complete recipes: a discovery tool from the family template, a parse-contract parser for a site, a catalog-driven search provider, an RSS/YouTube source, and git as the distribution vehicle.

roots.title: Security & Gotchas
roots.description: The T3 perimeter verbatim and what it means, keyring-sealed tokens, the SSRF posture, and why nothing auto-imports.

roots.title: Reference
roots.description: The vendored trio's API surface, the error taxonomy and its charter projection, tool-contract and status vocabularies, endpoints and limits.

roots.title: Versioning & Migration
roots.description: The extension/v1 envelope policy, append-only vocabularies, and the ADR-0035 sync law: vendored paths change via the dev canonical only.

roots.title: Troubleshooting & FAQ
roots.description: Extension problems decoded: server states, refresh failures, dropped rows, search errors.

children.title: Developer diagnostics & FAQ
children.description: Every wall-tested failure mode decoded — spawn errors, contract violations, provider taxonomy — plus the real FAQ.
